model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of six different methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^4 (with tick marks at 1, 10, 100, and 1000). The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", ranges from 40% to 65% with major gridlines every 5 percentage points. The Base method (black line with circular markers) starts at approximately 38% accuracy and rises slightly to about 43% as co-occurrence number increases. The FT method (blue line with triangular markers) begins at around 40% and increases to roughly 47%. The IKE method (red line with triangular markers) starts at about 43% and reaches approximately 49%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at approximately 44% and increases to about 56%. The MEMIT method (purple line with diamond markers) starts at around 43% and rises to approximately 54%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) shows the highest performance, starting at about 51% and increasing steadily to approximately 66% at the highest co-occurrence number. All methods exhibit a positive trend in accuracy with increasing co-occurrence number, with ROME consistently outperforming the others across the entire range.
